name: Uma Garcia

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a senior field researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We're independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government; we don't sell or campaign. Your answers are confidential, including the parts you wouldn't say at work. What is a normal day like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I manage twelve payroll specialists for a large cleaning-services company. We pay staff who work nights at depots and offices, and I spend too much of each pay week finding where a shift changed without reaching the payroll file. I have an MBA and I am one of the better people here at tracing a disputed payslip back to the original roster. I have never used an AI tool; I keep a paper correction log because it tells me who has been called back.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: And what is home like when the pay week ends?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and live with Tom, who works as a school caretaker, and our children, eight and twelve. We have a mortgage, my manager pay is high, and we have thirteen months of expenses saved. There are plenty of other large employers with payroll teams nearby. We need a new car eventually, but I won't order one before checking the household numbers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A little faster data entry would not change the work I get called for: someone has been paid the wrong shift rate and needs rent on Friday. My salary is high, Tom's school-caretaker pay is steady, and we have thirteen months of expenses saved. The mortgage feels manageable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our payroll team to keep the original shift sheet with every correction. I'd tell the depot supervisors that a worker needs a named person to call about missing pay. I have never used an AI tool, and I wouldn't tell them a quick new screen has solved a wage dispute.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know our pay rules well enough to find a missing night premium in a pile of slips. Our reserve and the number of large employers nearby make this role feel safe in a plateau, even if the software changes the forms. I want the children to see that we correct a mistake rather than hide it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next pay cycle I'll audit the nine corrected night-shift slips against the original depot rosters before they go to the bank. Through the plateau's first year I'll keep the phone line for pay disputes and move 250 monthly into our mortgage reserve while both wages cover the mortgage and school costs. I'd leave the new AI button alone unless the company explains its controls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm. A slow software year still has ordinary work for a careful payroll team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was wrong with a night premium?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A supervisor moved a cleaner to a late shift but the roster export still showed the old time. The cleaner called me because the short pay was the week's food money. A payroll line is somebody's dinner, not a neat number.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep thirteen months in reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tom and I had both seen colleagues wait for jobs after a site closed. We built the reserve before paying extra on the mortgage; it is not sitting there by accident. Our children are eight and twelve, and school bills come on their own schedule.

say: I'd tell payroll to keep **original shift sheets** with corrections.
I'd tell depot staff to keep a **named pay contact** for workers.
think: My **payroll expertise** still matters in a mild-change world.
Thirteen months saved and nearby employers make **my wage feel secure**.
do: Audit **nine corrected night-shift slips** against depot rosters next pay cycle.
Keep the **pay-dispute phone line** through the first plateau year.
Save **250 monthly** only while both wages cover mortgage and school costs.
feel: I feel **calm** about our work and household bills.
S0.quote: A payroll line is somebody's dinner, not a neat number.
fieldNote: She traces a missing premium to the **original roster**, not a polished screen.
High pay and **thirteen months cash** make the plateau secure for her.
The savings transfer depends on **both wages** paying regular bills.

steps.text: Audit nine corrected night-shift slips against original depot rosters next pay cycle
Save 250 monthly only while both wages cover mortgage and school costs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing pay explanations, checking rosters, planning the cycle and answering workers fill most of my team's hours. A stronger system could do much of that and leave us with a few unusual disputes. The cleaners still work on site, but my payroll desk is all records and decisions.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the company must publish how a worker contests a wrong payslip before cutting any phone hours. I'd ask the finance director for a parallel run on old payroll, with every difference listed. I would not promise my twelve specialists their shifts are safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can see my senior post being combined with another payroll region if the system checks most slips. I have an MBA and know the rules, but I don't use AI and would need someone else to demonstrate a new tool before I could judge it. Tom's wage and our thirteen-month reserve mean I can look carefully at other jobs, though my high salary is still at risk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January I'd request a paid two-cycle comparison of the new system with our old payroll, only if the finance director approves and a trained analyst runs the new tool beside me. I'd keep the pay-dispute phone line open and ask for a written staffing decision after the comparison. I'd apply for posted payroll manager jobs at the four nearby large employers after checking their wages and hours, staying at this company until a signed offer covers mortgage, food and school costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own post, but I am not without choices. I would rather read a bad comparison than a reassuring sales slide.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the comparison look for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The night premium and the missing meal allowance are my first two checks. If the tool pays one cleaner short, the analyst shows me why before anyone calls it ready. A payroll pilot is not a pay packet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try the tool yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after a trained analyst has shown me the controls on paid time and finance has approved the trial. I have not used AI; I am not going to learn it on a live payroll run. I can judge the wage outcome with the old roster beside me.

say: I'd demand a **pay dispute route** before phone hours shrink.
I'd request a **parallel payroll comparison** before staffing changes.
think: My **senior payroll post** could merge with another region.
Thirteen months cash permits a careful search, though **my high wage** is exposed.
do: Request a **paid two-cycle comparison**; run only with finance approval and trained analyst, then seek written staffing decision.
Apply for **posted nearby payroll roles** after checking pay and hours; leave only for an affordable signed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my role despite other options.
S1.quote: A payroll pilot is not a pay packet.
fieldNote: Her reluctance to use AI does not erase **strong payroll skill**.
She wants the night premium tested in a **paid parallel run**.
She keeps current pay until an **affordable signed offer** exists.

steps.text: Request paid two-cycle comparison; run only with finance approval and trained analyst, then seek staffing decision
Apply for nearby payroll roles with viable pay and hours; leave only after affordable signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 AGI could check every roster, calculate pay, answer workers and explain the rule better than our desk. I would expect the payroll management layer to shrink or disappear, including my role. Tom's hands-on caretaker work is physical until capable robots arrive around 2031, although his schedules and stock orders change in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the twelve specialists that 2028 is the date in this picture and ask for written notice terms. I'd tell workers to keep copies of their rosters and pay records. I'd tell Tom we should stop discussing a new car until we know what wage I still have.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my high payroll salary could go, but I cannot say no company will keep a human sign-off post. Tom's pay and thirteen months saved would cover the mortgage while I look, and many local employers might still post jobs, though their payroll work faces AGI too. I would worry about finding pay as good as this, not whether we eat next week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'd request written notice and severance figures from human resources and keep the thirteen-month reserve liquid. We'd postpone the new-car order before paying a deposit. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post ends, I'd apply for posted paid roles nearby after checking actual duties and pay, taking one only if its wage with Tom's confirmed pay covers mortgage, food and school costs; I'd leave my current wage only for a signed offer if the post still exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a major salary loss, but I can search with our reserve intact. I do not need to accept a misleading job title in haste.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would another payroll desk shelter you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Full AGI could do the same roster and calculation work at the four nearby employers. I would consider a real offered wage for the period it pays, not tell my partner Tom that a new employer makes the work permanent. The physical cleaning and repairs at his school could change with robots around 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How old would the children be?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They would be ten and fourteen in 2028. We would tell them the new car can wait and their school costs are covered. I will not make them responsible for my job search.

I'd tell workers to keep **roster and pay copies**.
think: My **high payroll salary** could go, though a human sign-off post may remain.
Tom's pay and thirteen months cash give me **search time** without immediate bill fear.
do: Request **written severance figures** from human resources now.
Postpone the **new-car deposit** until my wage is clear.
Apply for **posted nearby paid work** after checking duties; accept only an affordable signed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about replacing my salary while the mortgage is covered.
S2.quote: I would consider a real offered wage for the period it pays, not tell my partner Tom that a new employer makes the work permanent.
fieldNote: She expects a possible **large wage loss** but has time to search.
Nearby payroll desks also face **2028 AGI**, so vacancies are not automatic safety.
The new car is postponed **before its deposit**, preserving liquid cash.

steps.text: Request written payroll notice and severance figures before deciding next move
Postpone new-car deposit until manager wage is clear
Apply for posted nearby jobs; accept only signed offer with combined pay covering family bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives us time to lower the mortgage while my wage is still coming in. Payroll checking and dispute explanations face AGI in 2031. Tom still has hands-on school repairs until capable robots arrive around 2034, but his purchasing lists and schedules change in 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the finance director to set dates for payroll staffing decisions, not leave people guessing for years. I'd tell Tom we can pay extra on the mortgage without using our cash reserve. I'd tell workers where to keep their pay records.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may be paid as a payroll manager until 2031, and that is worth protecting. I am not eager to change tools for the sake of it, but I can compare posted jobs while there is time. The thirteen-month reserve and Tom's wage let us choose, although a lower salary after AGI would still change our monthly budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next year I'd pay 600 extra monthly on mortgage principal only while both wages cover school costs and thirteen months of expenses remain in cash. I'd ask the finance director for a written annual staffing date and keep applying to posted nearby roles only where the pay and hours are viable; I would not resign without a signed offer. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if my payroll post ends I'd take a paid local role only if its wage with Tom's confirmed pay covers mortgage, food and school costs, using the cash reserve to search if none does.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the wage after 2031, but the five years are useful. I can make the mortgage smaller without trying to guess the winning company.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Tom loses caretaker hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The 600 extra mortgage payment stops first. We keep the thirteen months in cash and pay the ordinary mortgage from confirmed income. I will not trade liquid money for a slightly smaller bill while one wage is uncertain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your team each year?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show the staffing date the finance director has actually signed, if there is one. If the company refuses to give a date, I would say that plainly. A calendar I invented cannot protect twelve payroll specialists.

I'd tell workers to keep **pay records** as systems change.
think: I may keep my payroll wage until 2031, but **later pay** is uncertain.
Cash and Tom's wage let us choose without assuming a **safe desk elsewhere**.
do: Pay **600 extra monthly** on mortgage only while both wages cover school, Tom's hours hold and thirteen months cash stays untouched.
Request a **signed annual staffing date** from finance.
Apply for **posted nearby work** only with viable pay and hours; leave after signed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my future wage while able to plan.
S3.quote: A calendar I invented cannot protect twelve payroll specialists.
fieldNote: She refuses to invent a **staffing guarantee** for twelve payroll specialists.
Mortgage overpayments stop if **Tom's hours** fall.
She treats local job listings as **possible wages**, not AGI protection.

steps.text: Pay 600 extra on mortgage if Tom's hours hold, school paid and thirteen months cash untouched
Request signed annual payroll staffing date from finance
Apply for posted nearby work with viable pay and hours; leave only after signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll be 53 in 2036, our younger child eighteen and older one twenty-two. They may live elsewhere, and I can't count either child's future pay. Payroll decisions face AGI in 2036, while Tom's physical school repairs face capable robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the company to publish its payroll transition dates and how workers dispute wrong pay. I'd tell Tom we should check our mortgage and cash once a year. I'd tell the children we can help with school if wages permit, without promising a blank cheque.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years could let us clear much of the mortgage if the high salary continues. I would still expect the payroll manager role to change by 2036, and I don't want to learn AI merely to defend a title. With savings and plenty of nearby employers, I could compare offers before deciding what to do with the house.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Beginning next spring I'd ask two estate agents for written sale estimates and compare them with the mortgage balance; I would not list our home now. I'd pay 700 extra monthly on the mortgage only while both wages cover school costs and thirteen months cash stays available, stopping if Tom's hours fall. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if no posted job pays enough, Tom and I would consider a smaller home only after the younger child finishes school, both of us agree and a real sale price covers the remaining mortgage and replacement housing; I would keep applying for affordable paid work meanwhile.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the decade ahead, not desperate. The house gives us choices only if we use real prices and leave the children's plans intact.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you tell your children you might move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not as a decision now. The younger will be eighteen in 2036 and may still be in school; the older will be twenty-two. We would talk before any move, and Tom and I would not sell until the numbers and schooling work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why get sale estimates so early?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I want to know whether the house is actually an option if my wage falls. An estimate is not a buyer, and a buyer is not a replacement home. I would rather have the arithmetic in a folder before a hurried decision.

I'd tell Tom we should check **mortgage and cash** yearly.
think: A continued high wage could reduce **mortgage debt** before 2036.
I would compare local offers before any **house decision**.
do: Get **two written sale estimates** next spring without listing the house.
Pay **700 extra monthly** on mortgage only while both wages cover school bills, thirteen months cash remains and Tom's hours hold.
Consider **2036 downsizing** only if no job pays enough, younger finishes school, Tom agrees and real sale funds mortgage and replacement housing.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about the payroll desk but able to plan.
S4.quote: An estimate is not a buyer, and a buyer is not a replacement home.
fieldNote: A house move is **conditional**, not an announced plan.
Her mortgage payments preserve **thirteen months cash** and stop if Tom's hours fall.
She will not use **adult children's unknown wages** to fund the mortgage.

steps.text: Get two written home sale estimates next spring without listing the house

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my payroll wage could vanish quickly. Written notice and severance figures, an actual paid opening with wages that cover our household, and a way for workers to contest wrong pay would help. Thirteen months saved lets us wait for an honest offer without pretending every local payroll desk is safe.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the cleaner with a short payslip whether a system explanation paid for dinner. The roster can be correct and the bank transfer still wrong. I need to know the money arrived before I close a pay case.

headlineQuote: The roster can be correct and the bank transfer still wrong.
portrait: Uma, **43**, leads twelve payroll specialists at a large cleaning-services company and holds an MBA.
She has never used AI, but her **payroll skill** traces disputed wages back to original shift rosters.
High pay, Tom's caretaker wage and **thirteen months saved** support two school-age children and a mortgage.
She tests real pay and house numbers before acting, while knowing **payroll desks face AGI**.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her high payroll wage before she finds an affordable replacement.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written notice and severance** figures and a real paid opening that covers household costs.
She wants a **pay dispute route** for workers whose bank transfer is wrong.
